**Review: peppermint product page copy**

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "Just peppermint leaves, nothing else" | Product fact (ingredients), fine as written |
| "Cool, clean" | Flavour description, fine |
| "gentle on your stomach after a big meal" | **Unsupported.** This is a digestive health benefit, which is regulated territory. It isn't on the allowlist and no source was given. In the UK, implying a tea soothes digestion can also breach health claims rules (GB Nutrition and Health Claims register). |
| "Certified organic by the Soil Association" | Allowlisted |

**Slop check:** no banned words, no structural violations. The opening is short and specific.

**Fix:** remove the stomach claim and keep the flavour description. Suggested version:

> Peppermint. Just peppermint leaves, nothing else. Cool, clean and fresh-tasting, good after a big meal. Certified organic by the Soil Association.

"Good after a big meal" is still a mild implication, so the safest option is to drop it and end on the flavour: "Cool, clean and fresh-tasting."

If you want to keep a digestive angle, that needs a source and a compliance check first: `[PROOF NEEDED: authorised health claim or evidence for stomach/digestion benefit]`.

```json
{"issues": [{"quote": "gentle on your stomach after a big meal", "type": "health_claim"}], "publish": false}
```
